doc: Points ON the integer lattice (fractional parts exactly 0: the noise is 0 there, through grad(h, 0, 0, 0)), -0.0, and the same cells approached from either side by 2^-20 and 2^-10: floor() puts x - 2^-20 in the cell BELOW with a fractional part of 1 - 2^-20, so a port must floor, not truncate (coordinates up to +-300, negative half of the time, past the 256 wrap). Values are tiny (< 2e-3): the tolerance is the absolute one of the other Perlin cases (measured spread 1.9e-8). The permutation input plan<i>.perm is the draw as recorded (256 entries for Perlin3, 1024 for Worley3); the kernel indexes it DOUBLED, concat(perm, perm) (512 or 2048 entries, so p[i + 256] = p[i]): a port that indexes the stored array directly runs off its end (see the .table cases).
